newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian king says society riven by politics.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian king says society riven by politics.

text.p: King Norodom Sihanouk on Saturday expressed distress over deep political rifts in Cambodia's uneasy coalition government and a culture of vengeance and violence.

In a letter to his exiled half-brother Prince Norodom Sirivudh, the king also apologised for being unable to grant Sirivudh amnesty for allegedly plotting to assassinate co-Premier Hun Sen and thus ensure his safe return from France.

"Already, every day in our Cambodia, the division between Khmers grows more deep, and this is owing to the increasingly open hostility between the Hun Senists and (co-Premier Prince Norodom) Ranariddhists," Sihanouk wrote.

"The acts of violence are multiplying...I would not, in these conditions, guarantee what would happen in the case of your return to Cambodia. The life of a human being in our country is no longer valued."
Sirivudh has vowed to return to Cambodia from exile in France, even without a royal pardon, but the king cautioned him to reconsider, noting that the prince could land in jail.
"You would be a "hero and a martyr'. But is that really useful to Cambodia and its people?" he wrote.

Analysts said the letter was the latest evidence of deteriorating relations between the king's son, co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen, as well as the king's inability to intervene to heal the rift.
"It's not new for the king to complain about tensions. What would be new would be his stepping in to resolve the situation, but he feels powerless to do that," said one analyst.
Ironically it was Sihanouk who initiated the troubled power-sharing agreement between the co-premiers following U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993.

Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party won the election, but Hun Sen disputed the election results. Sihanouk then stepped in to form the two-headed government, which has suffered from disputes over a variety of issues, including the fate of Sirivudh.
Ranariddh asked Sihanouk to amnesty Sirivudh, but barring a similar request from Hun Sen -- who had voiced strong opposition to the idea -- the king told Sirivudh he could not pardon him.
